title: Zach Yadegari: Paying MrBeast $500K, decision frameworks, and how to validate app ideas
summary: Zach Yadegari explains how Cal AI paid MrBeast $500K for a sponsorship that roughly broke even short-term and paid off through credibility. He also covers using expected value to decide on selling a company, validating ideas against proven adjacent apps, and surviving an uncertain AI future.

principles.text: Judge influencer sponsorships by long-term credibility, not just direct return; big-name association unlocks later deals.
principles.quote: having the brand name Mr. Be saying we were in a video, we were able to do way more deals afterwards. We had way more credibility with our brand

principles.text: Attribution for creator ads is fuzzy; triangulate with time overlap and promo code usage.
principles.quote: looking at the time overlap, looking at promo code usage, and a few other metrics that we used to determine this stuff, we probably made $350,000, maybe $400,000 just from that $500,000 promo.

principles.text: Use expected value (probability times prize, including the chance of collapse) to decide whether to sell versus keep going.
principles.quote: the percent chance of winning something and then the prize and you multiply them together.

principles.text: Learning to validate ideas matters more than generating them, and validation should fit your own skills and firsthand experience.
principles.quote: learning how to come up with ideas. That is a skill. But I think the more important skill and the better skill is a framework to validate what is a good idea

principles.text: A competitor already earning big revenue is proof of demand and sets a floor for your ceiling; don't be deterred by 'it already exists'.
principles.quote: this other app is making $200 million a year. So, I know that's like the se like the minimum ceiling, the lowest floor of what we could get to.

principles.text: Favor ideas that are highly marketable and viral, in problems you've personally experienced or whose users you know.
principles.quote: I look for ideas that I know are very marketable. They can go super viral. And I look for things that I've personally experienced
